title: Adentris vs Supanote: Behavioral Health Documentation Compared
summary: Adentris vs Supanote for behavioral health and SUD: an AI therapy scribe versus real-time revenue integrity, ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth, and an appeals and denials module.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Supanote and Adentris both work in behavioral health documentation, but they solve different halves of the problem. Supanote is an AI scribe that generates mental-health progress notes from recorded, uploaded, or dictated sessions in formats like SOAP, DAP, and BIRP. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note, however it was written, in real time before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module built in. If your problem is note-writing time, Supanote is built for that. If your problem is denials and audit exposure, that is where Adentris focuses.


Both touch the therapy note, so the honest comparison is about which problem you are solving: writing it or getting it paid. Here is the breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is not a scribe: it does not write the note, it makes sure the note will get paid. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What Supanote does


Supanote is an AI scribe purpose-built for behavioral health that generates therapy progress notes from recorded, uploaded, or dictated sessions, supporting a wide range of formats including SOAP, DAP, and BIRP. It is designed to cut documentation time for therapists and counselors. For clinicians who want fast, mental-health-specific notes, Supanote is a strong, focused option.

## Which should you choose?


Supanote is built to generate the behavioral health note quickly across many formats. Adentris is built for a different job: catching the documentation gaps that get behavioral health and SUD claims denied and fixing them before submission. It flags a missing medical necessity statement, an unjustified ASAM level of care, or a missing 42 CFR Part 2 consent, drafts the correction while the note is open, and supports the appeal if a payer denies. For SUD programs, ASAM and Part 2 depth, real-time pre-submission timing, and running on any EHR through a secure web agent are the practical differences. A clinician can use Supanote to write the note and Adentris to make sure it gets paid.


- **Choose Supanote if** you want fast, mental-health-specific notes generated from your sessions across formats like SOAP, DAP, and BIRP.
- **Choose Adentris if** your problem is not writing the note but getting it paid: you want the documentation checked against payer and regulatory denial criteria before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and an appeals workflow, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a Supanote alternative for revenue integrity


If your practice uses Supanote, or is evaluating it, and the gap you feel is not note-writing time but denied claims and audit exposure, that is a different job. Adentris reviews the finished documentation against payer and regulatory denial criteria, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs that with an appeals and denials workflow. It runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, so it fits alongside a scribe rather than replacing it. For clinicians who write notes well but still lose claims, it is a natural complement.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. Supanote is a strong, mental-health-specific scribe. If your losses come from denied claims rather than slow notes, Adentris reviews the finished note before submission for ASAM and Part 2 gaps and pairs it with appeals, on any EHR.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and Supanote?**


Supanote is an AI scribe that generates mental-health progress notes from sessions in formats like SOAP, DAP, and BIRP. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note in real time before the claim is submitted, drafts corrections, and has SUD-specific rules like ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals module built in. Supanote helps write the note; Adentris makes sure it gets paid.


**Can Adentris and Supanote be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use Supanote to generate the progress note and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside Supanote.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to Supanote?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than note-writing time, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. Supanote is strong for fast, mental-health-specific note generation. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
